pred_ddx.label: Primary Biliary Cirrhosis-associated Porphyria Cutanea Tarda

Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris: The patient's presentation of pruritic eruption with dusky, thin plaques and a central collarette of scale, along with hyperkeratotic plaques and deeply seated vesicles on the hands and feet, is consistent with Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris. The laboratory findings and punch biopsy results also support this diagnosis, particularly the presence of psoriasiform epidermal acanthosis and hyperkeratosis.

The laboratory results showing elevated bilirubin and liver enzymes also support this diagnosis, as Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris can be associated with liver disease.
Primary Biliary Cirrhosis-associated Por: The patient's history of alcoholic cirrhosis, scleral icterus, and elevated bilirubin levels, combined with the skin findings of hyperkeratotic plaques and vesicles with a greenish-black hue, suggest a possible diagnosis of Primary Biliary Cirrhosis-associated Porphyria Cutanea Tarda. The punch biopsy findings of dilated eccrine ducts containing amorphous pink material also support this diagnosis.
